title: Dedicated throughput SLO: add burn-rate alerts + wire to paging policies
author: Aisha Bello
description: Context: As part of Dedicated throughput guarantees, we need first-class SLO alerting that is (a) burn-rate based (fast/slow), (b) scoped per Dedicated deployment, and (c) correctly routed to oncall + CS escalation paths. This PR adds burn-rate alert rules for the Dedicated Throughput Floor SLO and wires them into our paging policies. It also adds the runbook links and dashboard deep-links to make the alerts actionable. Scope: - New Prometheus rules for Dedicated throughput SLO burn-rate (page + ticket) - Tier-aware routing labels (Standard/Plus/Premium) to support different urgency/paging - Alertmanager routes + PagerDuty service mapping (SRE oncall; non-page tickets to #customer-success triage) - Annotations: customer/deployment identifiers, region, model, and links to the Dedicated Throughput dashboard panels - Guardrails: suppress alerts when deployment is in provisioning/warmup window or explicitly marked 'customer_throttled' by admission-control telemetry Notes: The burn-rate computations follow the SLO Toolkit conventions (fast: 2h window, slow: 24h window) but are implemented using Redwood’s in-repo rule templates to avoid an additional dependency at runtime. Related: ENG-19244 (metric emission), ENG-19257 (tier-aware admission control).
commits: sre/alerts: add dedicated_throughput_slo burn-rate recording rules
alertmanager: route dedicated throughput pages to SRE PD + add ticket route
dashboards: add dedicated dashboard links + runbook annotations
config: tier label mapping + warmup suppression conditions
docs: update oncall handbook section for Dedicated throughput pages
checks: CI: build (pass) | unit tests (pass) | alerts lint/validate (pass) | jsonnet (pass) | prometheus rule unit tests (pass) | security scan (pass)
conversation:
Rafael Mendes (review): Can you confirm these are burn-rate alerts (multi-window, multi-burn) and not just thresholding on tokens/sec? We should avoid paging on transient dips if error budget isn’t burning.

Aisha Bello (author): Yep. The rule fires on burn rate of the SLO ratio (good/total over windows). Fast path is 2h window, slow path is 24h; page requires both fast+slow burn to reduce noise. The underlying SLI is still tokens/sec floor vs observed, but we alert on the error-budget burn.

Sean Gallagher (review): Please link the canonical SLO name/id in the annotations so SLO reporting can join on it. Also, can we add explicit exclusions for (1) provisioning/warm pool period and (2) customer-side throttling / 429s?

Aisha Bello (author): Added `slo_id: dedicated.throughput_floor` annotation + updated the suppressor to ignore the first 20m after `deployment_ready=true`. For customer throttling, I added a suppression predicate when `dedicated_admission_denied_total{reason="customer_quota"}` dominates and `request_rate` is below committed (i.e., they aren’t sending).

Allison Grant (review): Routing: for now, please keep all pages going to SRE PD. If we want tier-specific paging later, encode tier as a label but don’t create multiple PD services until we see volume.

Aisha Bello (author): Ack. I kept a single PD service (`pd-sre-primary`) and added `tier` label purely for context + future routing. Ticket route goes to Slack triage channel + creates Opsgenie ticket via webhook.

Sergio Costa (review): Dashboard deep-link should land on the per-deployment panel with deployment_id pre-filtered. Also: use the public dashboard slug (not the internal jsonnet path).

Aisha Bello (author): Updated annotations to use `https://console.redwoodinference.com/ops/dedicated/throughput?deployment_id={{ $labels.deployment_id }}` which resolves to the correct panel view.

Rafael Mendes (follow-up): Can you add rule unit tests with a synthetic time series showing a sustained burn vs a transient dip?

Aisha Bello (author): Added promtool-style tests in `tests/alerts/test_dedicated_throughput_rules.py` for (1) sustained under-floor => page, (2) short dip => no page, (3) warmup window => suppressed.

Sean Gallagher (approval): Looks good. One nit: set `severity=page` only for the multiwindow condition; keep the single-window signal as `severity=ticket` to avoid paging on partial data.

Aisha Bello (author): Done (split into `DedicatedThroughputSLOBurnRateHigh` (page) and `DedicatedThroughputSLOBurnRateElevated` (ticket)).

Rafael Mendes (approval): Approved.

Allison Grant (approval): Approved once lint passes.

CI rerun: alerts lint failed due to missing runbook link for ticket alert; fixed in follow-up commit. All checks green.
release_notes: Dedicated: Added burn-rate alerting for throughput floor SLO and wired paging/ticket routing with runbook + dashboard links.
